title: Configuration for Statistical Models — configurar_prioris
text: hyperparameters control strength assumptions regarding latent state evolution, institute bias, non-sampling errors. Variable names refer model notation described https://rnmag.github.io/agregR/index.html#conceptual-framework Recommended reading: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/prior-choice-recommendations State Model - Level (\(\mu\)) mu_priori: Prior mean latent vote share \(t=1\). sd_mu_priori: Prior uncertainty initial latent vote. Default values: \(\mu\) starts flat prior N(0.5, 0.5), allowing data quickly dominate inference. omega_eta_priori: Prior mean level volatility (\(\omega_\eta\)). sd_omega_eta_priori: Prior uncertainty level volatility. Default values: omega_eta_priori = 0.002 sd_omega_eta_priori = 0.0001, model assumes baseline drift approx. \(\pm 2\) percentage points month (\(1.96 \times \sqrt{30} \times 0.002 \approx 0.02\)). Higher values: latent vote (\(\mu\)) can jump one day next. model adapts quickly new polls becomes "jittery". Lower values: model assumes public opinion level stable time, resulting smoother curves. State Model - Trend (\(\nu\)) nu_priori: Prior mean initial trend (daily growth rate). sd_nu_priori: Prior uncertainty initial trend. Default values: nu_priori = 0 sd_nu_priori = 0.001, model expects initial trend within \(\pm 0.2\) percentage points per day (\(1.96 \times 0.001 \approx 0.002\)). omega_zeta_priori: Prior mean trend volatility (\(\omega_\zeta\)). sd_omega_zeta_priori: Prior uncertainty trend volatility. Default values: omega_zeta_priori = 0 sd_omega_zeta_priori = 0.00001, model assumes linear evolution, allowing trend shift rapidly (accelerations) strong evidence. Higher values: trend (\(\nu\)) can change direction magnitude rapidly. Lower values: trend assumed constant time (linear evolution). Institute Bias (\(\delta\)) delta_priori: Mean expected bias institutes. Default 0, except "Viés Empírico" anchored past performance. sd_delta_priori: Scale bias prior. Default values: delta_priori = 0 sd_delta_priori = 0.02, model assumes 95% institutes bias within \(\pm 4\) percentage points (\(1.96 \times 0.02 \approx 0.04\)). Higher values: Allow larger, variable biases across institutes. Lower values: Constrain institutes similar biases (shrinkage toward anchor). Non-Sampling Error (\(\tau\)) tau_priori: Mean expected magnitude errors explained sampling house effects. weighted models, replaced empirical RMSE past elections. sd_tau_priori: Prior uncertainty non-sampling error. Default values: tau_priori = 0.02 sd_tau_priori = 0.02, model assumes baseline \(\pm 4\) percentage points "noise" poll, allowing spread closer \(\pm 7\) percentage points. Higher values: model treats polls less precise, widening credible intervals latent state. Lower values: model trusts polling precision , leading tighter intervals potentially sensitivity outliers.

title: Run Poll Aggregator — rodar_agregador
text: aggregator supports five types Bayesian state-space models, specific assumptions institute bias non-sampling errors: 1. Viés Relativo com Pesos (Default) Assumption: Institute biases relative average institutes (latent "truth" anchored consensus). Bias (\(\delta\)): Calculated relative mean bias institutes. Weights (\(\tau\)): Uses past election performance weight non-sampling error. Institutes larger historical errors less influence current estimate. Use case: Best general forecasting historical data available. 2. Viés Relativo sem Pesos Assumption: , treats institutes equal potential quality priori. Bias (\(\delta\)): Calculated relative mean bias. Weights (\(\tau\)): None. institutes share prior non-sampling error. Use case: historical data unreliable "fresh start" assumption desired. 3. Viés Empírico Assumption: Institute biases anchored specific historical performance. Bias (\(\delta\)): Prior means set bias observed previous election (directional error). Weights (\(\tau\)): Uses past performance non-sampling error, similar "Com Pesos" model. Use case: institutes expected repeat specific past directional errors (e.g., consistently underestimating specific wing). 4. Retrospectivo Assumption: true election result known used final anchor state-space model. Method: Runs model "backwards" constrained final result estimate true path public opinion. Use case: Post-election analysis diagnose institute performance calculate accurate biases future calibration. 5. Naive Assumption: Polls bias non-sampling error. Method: random walk model source uncertainty sampling error (\(\sigma\)). Use case: Baseline comparison. Assumes "polls perfect" within margin error.

text: config_prioris argument allows customization model's hyperparameters configurar_prioris() function. hyperparameters control strength assumptions regarding latent state evolution, institute bias, non-sampling errors. Variable names refer model notation described https://rnmag.github.io/agregR/index.html#conceptual-framework Recommended reading: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/prior-choice-recommendations State Model - Level (\(\mu\)) mu_priori: Prior mean latent vote share \(t=1\). sd_mu_priori: Prior uncertainty initial latent vote. Default values: \(\mu\) starts flat prior N(0.5, 0.5), allowing data quickly dominate inference. omega_eta_priori: Prior mean level volatility (\(\omega_\eta\)). sd_omega_eta_priori: Prior uncertainty level volatility. Default values: omega_eta_priori = 0.002 sd_omega_eta_priori = 0.0001, model assumes baseline drift approx. \(\pm 2\) percentage points month (\(1.96 \times \sqrt{30} \times 0.002 \approx 0.02\)). Higher values: latent vote (\(\mu\)) can jump one day next. model adapts quickly new polls becomes "jittery". Lower values: model assumes public opinion level stable time, resulting smoother curves. State Model - Trend (\(\nu\)) nu_priori: Prior mean initial trend (daily growth rate). sd_nu_priori: Prior uncertainty initial trend. Default values: nu_priori = 0 sd_nu_priori = 0.001, model expects initial trend within \(\pm 0.2\) percentage points per day (\(1.96 \times 0.001 \approx 0.002\)). omega_zeta_priori: Prior mean trend volatility (\(\omega_\zeta\)). sd_omega_zeta_priori: Prior uncertainty trend volatility. Default values: omega_zeta_priori = 0 sd_omega_zeta_priori = 0.00001, model assumes linear evolution, allowing trend shift rapidly (accelerations) strong evidence. Higher values: trend (\(\nu\)) can change direction magnitude rapidly. Lower values: trend assumed constant time (linear evolution). Institute Bias (\(\delta\)) delta_priori: Mean expected bias institutes. Default 0, except "Viés Empírico" anchored past performance. sd_delta_priori: Scale bias prior. Default values: delta_priori = 0 sd_delta_priori = 0.02, model assumes 95% institutes bias within \(\pm 4\) percentage points (\(1.96 \times 0.02 \approx 0.04\)). Higher values: Allow larger, variable biases across institutes. Lower values: Constrain institutes similar biases (shrinkage toward anchor). Non-Sampling Error (\(\tau\)) tau_priori: Mean expected magnitude errors explained sampling house effects. weighted models, replaced empirical RMSE past elections. sd_tau_priori: Prior uncertainty non-sampling error. Default values: tau_priori = 0.02 sd_tau_priori = 0.02, model assumes baseline \(\pm 4\) percentage points "noise" poll, allowing spread closer \(\pm 7\) percentage points. Higher values: model treats polls less precise, widening credible intervals latent state. Lower values: model trusts polling precision , leading tighter intervals potentially sensitivity outliers.
